title: Commentary on 1 Thessalonians
english: The Christians in Thessalonica endured many persecutions from the Gentiles while the Greeks were still in power, which is what he uses to comfort them. He also remembers the resurrection of the dead, comforting them regarding the loss of their own [family members]. The prescribed thanksgiving in the preface is a testimony to the piety of the Thessalonians.

Faith stirs one toward the work of good (1 Thess 1:3), love enables one to endure hardships, and hope enables those struggling to endure with patience. Faith stirs one toward labors, and love enables one to persist in hardships.

Knowing, he says, beloved brothers, that the gospel did not come to you in word only, but also in power (1 Thess 1:4-5). Not only, he says, did we preach the word to you, but we also demonstrated powers and miracles to you (1 Thess 1:5). Instead of being passed on and proclaimed (1 Thess 1:8).

It was not permitted to us, he says, to be deprived of our boldness toward Christ by the evils in Philippi, but having come to you, we preached the word without shame (1 Thess 2:2). The gospel through which we exhort the afflicted—that is, the resurrection and the recompense within it—is preached not according to error but according to truth (1 Thess 2:4). Instead of being burdensome and oppressive because of demanding the honors which apostles of Christ ought to receive (1 Thess 2:7).
